examples.solution_text:
The products of the two intercepts of each chord are equal.

$\begin{aligned}AP\times PB&=CP\times PD\\16\times6&=12\times PD\\96&=12\times PD\\PD&=8\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

(a) Measure both intercepts from $P$. The far intercept includes the external part and the chord.

$\begin{aligned}PB&=PA+AB\\&=8+10\\&=18\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

The products of the secant intercepts are equal.

$\begin{aligned}PA\times PB&=PC\times PD\\8\times18&=6\times PD\\144&=6\times PD\\PD&=24\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

(b) Subtract the external part to find the chord.

$\begin{aligned}CD&=PD-PC\\&=24-6\\&=18\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

(a) The square of the tangent length equals the product of the near and far secant intercepts.

$\begin{aligned}PC^2&=PN\times PF\\12^2&=6\times PF\\144&=6\times PF\\PF&=24\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

(b) The chord excludes the external part.

$\begin{aligned}NF&=PF-PN\\&=24-6\\&=18\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

If the far intercept is given instead, use the same rule to find the near intercept before subtracting.

Apply the intersecting-chords rule, expand and collect the terms on one side.

$\begin{aligned}AP\times PB&=CP\times PD\\x(x+4)&=6\times8\\x^2+4x&=48\\x^2+4x-48&=0\end{aligned}$

In $\triangle EQH$ and $\triangle GQF$:

$\angle HEQ=\angle FGQ$, since both stand on chord $HF$.

$\angle EHQ=\angle GFQ$, since both stand on chord $EG$.

Therefore $\triangle EQH\sim\triangle GQF$ by equal corresponding angles.

Corresponding sides are proportional:

$\frac{EQ}{GQ}=\frac{QH}{QF}$.

Cross-multiplying gives $EQ\times QF=GQ\times QH$.

The secant rule gives $TE\times TF=TH\times TG$.

Since $TE=TH>0$, division gives $TF=TG$.

The chord lengths exclude the equal external parts:

$\begin{aligned}EF&=TF-TE\\HG&=TG-TH\end{aligned}$

Subtracting equal lengths from equal lengths gives $EF=HG$.

(a) The near intercept is $PN=h$. The far intercept includes the diameter, so $PF=h+2R$.

$\begin{aligned}PC^2&=PN\times PF\\d^2&=h(h+2R)\end{aligned}$

(b) Convert the radius to metres before substituting.

$R=6200\text{ km}=6\,200\,000\text{ m}$.

$\begin{aligned}d^2&=4(4+2\times6\,200\,000)\\&=4(12\,400\,004)\\&=49\,600\,016\end{aligned}$

Take the positive square root because $d$ is a length.

$d=\sqrt{49\,600\,016}\text{ m}\approx7043\text{ m}$.
